text: 3430 Bradfield (prov. designation: 1980 TF4) is a stony Sq-type asteroid from the central regions of the asteroid belt, with a diameter of approximately 8 kilometers (5 miles). It was discovered on 9 October 1980 by American astronomer Carolyn Shoemaker at the Palomar Observatory in California and is named after comet hunter William A. Bradfield (1927–2014), a New Zealand-born Australian amateur astronomer and rocket engineer who discovered several comets and significantly increased the rate of bright comet discoveries from the southern hemisphere during the 1970s and 1980s. The official naming citation was published by the Minor Planet Center on 14 April 1987 (M.P.C. 11750). According to the hierarchical clustering method by Nesvorný, Bradfield is a member of the Agnia family (514), a large group of stony asteroids with over 2000 known members, which likely formed from the breakup of a basalt object that originated from a larger parent body that underwent igneous differentiation; the family's parent body and namesake is asteroid 847 Agnia. However, in the 1995-HCM analysis by Zappalà, it is classified as a member of the Liberatrix family, also referred to as the Nemesis family by Nesvorný. Bradfield orbits the Sun in the central main belt at a distance of 2.5–3.0 AU, completing one orbit every 4 years and 7 months (1,674 days) with a semi-major axis of 2.76 AU, an orbital eccentricity of 0.10, and an inclination of 4° relative to the ecliptic. Its observation arc begins with records from 1974 HY1 at Cerro El Roble Observatory in April 1974, more than six years before its official discovery. In the SMASS classification, Bradfield is an Sq-subtype, transitioning between the common stony S-type and Q-type asteroids. Data from NASA's NEOWISE mission, part of the Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer, indicates that Bradfield has a diameter of 8.492 kilometers and a surface albedo of 0.269. As of 2018, no rotational lightcurve has been obtained for Bradfield, and its rotation period, pole orientation, and shape remain unknown.
